Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) is a method for combining multiple ranking signals into a unified ranking. For each item in each ranking, a score of 1/(k + rank) is computed, where k is a constant typically set to 60. An item present in both rankings receives contributions from both legs. The total scores are summed and items are sorted descending. RRF is particularly effective for hybrid search systems that combine a sparse keyword signal (BM25) with a dense vector signal (cosine similarity) because it is rank-based and thus does not require score normalization across different scoring scales.
